### **Claude** `00:06`

I've read the touched file and traced every new sink in the diff:

1. **`SEL_MANDOS` selector widening** (line 1060-1062): pure CSS selector for `querySelectorAll` — no injection surface, no sink.

2. **Guard block** (lines 1069-1091): iterates DOM elements from the same page, collects their `.id` values (statically defined in the HTML), builds `msg` from a hardcoded count plus those IDs, and writes to:
   - `console.error(...)` — not a sink
   - `d.style.cssText = '...static...'` — static literal, no interpolation
   - `d.textContent = msg.join(' · ')` — `textContent` (not `innerHTML`), XSS-safe even if IDs were tainted
   - `document.body.appendChild(d)` — appending a text-only div

3. **Provenance line** (line 1568): `document.getElementById('prov').textContent = '...static string...'` — static literal assigned via `textContent`. Safe.

The `_campos()` consolidation to reuse `SEL_MANDOS` (line 1316) just narrows scope; no new data source.

This is a local dev harness (`tools/banco-mapa/webroot/index.html`) with no server-side interaction added, no attacker-controlled input reaching any of the new code, and the only DOM writes use `textContent`/static style strings. No source→sink path with impact exists in this diff.

---

### **Claude** `00:50`

I've read the only touched application file (`frontend/app/_layout.tsx`) in full, and analyzed the two package-manifest changes in the diff.

Assessment of each changed file:

**`frontend/app/_layout.tsx`** — The only code change is removing the `duration: 220` argument from `RNBootSplash.hide({ fade: true })`. That property was already ignored by v6's `Config` type (per the added comment) and remains ignored by v7. No new sink, no new source, no entry-point change. The call is wrapped in `.catch(() => {})` and gated on `Platform.OS !== 'web'`. Nothing security-relevant.

**`frontend/package.json`**:
- `react-native-bootsplash` bumped `^6.3.10` → `^7.3.2` (major upgrade). This drops a large tree of `@react-native-community/cli-*` transitive deps and pulls in `sharp` — but `sharp` is used only by the library's build-time CLI, not at app runtime. No new runtime attack surface reachable from the app; no reintroduction of a known-vulnerable version.
- `shell-quote` override changed from pinned `1.8.4` → `^1.10.0`. This is a version *floor raise* (not a downgrade), and both endpoints are past the CVE-2021-42740 fix (1.7.3). A looser semver range on an override is not itself a vulnerability — it forbids anything below 1.10.0 and stays within 1.x.

**`frontend/package-lock.json`** — reflects the two dependency changes above; no bespoke, previously-unlocked packages were pinned to a vulnerable version. All added `@img/sharp-*` platform binaries are the current 0.35.4 line.

No source→sink path was introduced or weakened by this diff.

=== DIFF: scripts/servir-dist-local.py ===
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+"""Servidor local para VERIFICAR el bundle ANTES de desplegar.
+
+Uso:  python3 scripts/servir-dist-local.py     ->  http://127.0.0.1:8200/app/
+      LYAI_DIST=/otra/carpeta python3 scripts/servir-dist-local.py
+
+Sirve frontend/dist bajo /app/ y reenvia /api a ski.lyai.pro. Existe porque el 29-08
+desplegue una regresion (mapa centrado en [0,0]) por no poder mirarla antes."""
+import http.server, socketserver, urllib.request, urllib.error, os
+# 2026-08-30 · al mudarlo del scratchpad a scripts/ esta linea apuntaba a `scripts/local-www`,
+# que no existe: servia 404 sin decir por que. Ahora cuelga del repo, no del script.
+REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+RAIZ = os.environ.get('LYAI_DIST') or os.path.join(REPO, 'frontend', 'dist')
+ARRIBA = 'https://ski.lyai.pro'
+class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def __init__(self,*a,**k): super().__init__(*a, directory=RAIZ, **k)
+    def _proxy(self, cuerpo=None):
+        url = ARRIBA + self.path
+        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=cuerpo, method=self.command)
+        for h in ('content-type','accept','accept-language'):
+            if self.headers.get(h): req.add_header(h, self.headers[h])
+        try:
+            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
+                d=r.read(); self.send_response(r.status)
+                self.send_header('content-type', r.headers.get('content-type','application/json'))
+                self.send_header('access-control-allow-origin','*')
+                self.send_header('content-length', str(len(d))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(d)
+        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+            d=e.read(); self.send_response(e.code)
+            self.send_header('content-length',str(len(d))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(d)
+        except Exception:
+            self.send_response(502); self.end_headers()
+    def do_GET(self):
+        if self.path.startswith('/api'): return self._proxy()
+        # 2026-08-30 · `dist` tiene su index.html en la RAIZ, pero la app se sirve bajo /app/
+        # (asi vive en dev.lyai.pro). En el scratchpad esto lo resolvia una carpeta puente con
+        # un `app/` dentro; al traerlo al repo hay que quitar el prefijo aqui, o todo da 404
+        # y parece que el build esta roto cuando lo que esta mal es el servidor.
+        if self.path == '/app' or self.path.startswith('/app/'):
+            self.path = self.path[4:] or '/'
+        # el export de Expo genera chat.html, map.html… y sirve /app/chat sin extension.
+        # Sin esto, /app/chat da 404 en local y parece que la app esta rota cuando no lo esta.
+        import os as _o
+        ruta = self.path.split('?')[0]
+        if '.' not in ruta.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]:
+            f = _o.path.join(RAIZ, ruta.lstrip('/'))
+            if not _o.path.isdir(f) and not _o.path.exists(f) and _o.path.exists(f + '.html'):
+                self.path = ruta + '.html'
+        return super().do_GET()
+    def do_POST(self):
+        n=int(self.headers.get('content-length') or 0)
+        return self._proxy(self.rfile.read(n) if n else None)
+    def log_message(self,*a): pass
+socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer.allow_reuse_address=True
+with socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1',8200), H) as s: s.serve_forever()

Investigate per the method in your instructions, then return the findings list.

---

### **Claude** `00:51`

Looking at the changes, the main security-relevant surface is the new `scripts/servir-dist-local.py` — a local HTTP server that acts as a static file server for `frontend/dist` AND a proxy for `/api` requests to `https://ski.lyai.pro`. The other changes (bootsplash prop removal, dep bumps, package.json override loosening) don't introduce new sinks.

Let me trace the proxy's data flow:

**Entry point**: `do_GET`/`do_POST` on 127.0.0.1:8200
**Sink**: `urllib.request.urlopen(ARRIBA + self.path, ...)` sending to production API

Analysis of the proxy:
- Bound to 127.0.0.1 — good, only local origin
- Forwards `self.path` verbatim after `.startswith('/api')` — host is hardcoded so no SSRF host injection
- Does NOT forward cookies or auth headers (only content-type, accept, accept-language)
- Response sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`

The exploitable concern: while the dev runs this proxy, any website the developer's browser loads (in the same browser) can make cross-origin `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:8200/api/...")` calls. The proxy forwards them to production `ski.lyai.pro`, and because the response carries `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, the attacker page can READ the responses — a same-origin-policy bypass.

Impact bounds:
- Cookies aren't forwarded → cannot impersonate the dev
- BUT: the proxy strips the browser's `Origin`/`Referer` and requests appear from the developer's public IP → any endpoint on ski.lyai.pro that authorizes based on IP allowlisting, private-network reachability, or that returns data based on request origin, is exposed
- Preflight for non-simple requests (JSON POST) would fail since OPTIONS isn't handled, but simple GETs and form-encoded POSTs are exploitable
- Also serves as a stable CORS-bypass vector for anything ski.lyai.pro restricts by origin

This is a dev-only tool, but the risk window exists whenever it's running. Reporting at medium.

=== DIFF: scripts/servir-dist-local.py ===
@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+"""Servidor local para VERIFICAR el bundle ANTES de desplegar.
+
+Uso:  python3 scripts/servir-dist-local.py     ->  http://127.0.0.1:8200/app/
+      LYAI_DIST=/otra/carpeta python3 scripts/servir-dist-local.py
+
+Sirve frontend/dist bajo /app/ y reenvia /api a ski.lyai.pro. Existe porque el 29-08
+desplegue una regresion (mapa centrado en [0,0]) por no poder mirarla antes."""
+import http.server, socketserver, urllib.request, urllib.error, os
+# 2026-08-30 · al mudarlo del scratchpad a scripts/ esta linea apuntaba a `scripts/local-www`,
+# que no existe: servia 404 sin decir por que. Ahora cuelga del repo, no del script.
+REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+RAIZ = os.environ.get('LYAI_DIST') or os.path.join(REPO, 'frontend', 'dist')
+ARRIBA = 'https://ski.lyai.pro'
+class H(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def __init__(self,*a,**k): super().__init__(*a, directory=RAIZ, **k)
+    def _proxy(self, cuerpo=None):
+        url = ARRIBA + self.path
+        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=cuerpo, method=self.command)
+        for h in ('content-type','accept','accept-language'):
+            if self.headers.get(h): req.add_header(h, self.headers[h])
+        try:
+            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
+                d=r.read(); self.send_response(r.status)
+                self.send_header('content-type', r.headers.get('content-type','application/json'))
+                self.send_header('access-control-allow-origin','*')
+                self.send_header('content-length', str(len(d))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(d)
+        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
+            d=e.read(); self.send_response(e.code)
+            self.send_header('content-length',str(len(d))); self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(d)
+        except Exception:
+            self.send_response(502); self.end_headers()
+    def do_GET(self):
+        if self.path.startswith('/api'): return self._proxy()
+        # 2026-08-30 · `dist` tiene su index.html en la RAIZ, pero la app se sirve bajo /app/
+        # (asi vive en dev.lyai.pro). En el scratchpad esto lo resolvia una carpeta puente con
+        # un `app/` dentro; al traerlo al repo hay que quitar el prefijo aqui, o todo da 404
+        # y parece que el build esta roto cuando lo que esta mal es el servidor.
+        if self.path == '/app' or self.path.startswith('/app/'):
+            self.path = self.path[4:] or '/'
+        # el export de Expo genera chat.html, map.html… y sirve /app/chat sin extension.
+        # Sin esto, /app/chat da 404 en local y parece que la app esta rota cuando no lo esta.
+        import os as _o
+        ruta = self.path.split('?')[0]
+        if '.' not in ruta.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]:
+            f = _o.path.join(RAIZ, ruta.lstrip('/'))
+            if not _o.path.isdir(f) and not _o.path.exists(f) and _o.path.exists(f + '.html'):
+                self.path = ruta + '.html'
+        return super().do_GET()
+    def do_POST(self):
+        n=int(self.headers.get('content-length') or 0)
+        return self._proxy(self.rfile.read(n) if n else None)
+    def log_message(self,*a): pass
+socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer.allow_reuse_address=True
+with socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer(('127.0.0.1',8200), H) as s: s.serve_forever()

### **Claude** `01:05`

Analysis:

**Change summary**: Removed `station_id` filter from both the Mongo and Postgres branches of `fetch_active_alerts`. All active alerts are now returned regardless of the user's resort context.

**Sinks touched**:
- Mongo query `mdb.alerts.find({"active": True}, ...)` — no user input interpolated
- Postgres query built as an f-string with `where` — but `where` is now a static literal (no user input), and `params` list is empty
- Output is a formatted string joined into LLM context

**Data flow**:
- No new attacker-controlled input flows into either query. `q` is a static dict; `where` is a static string.
- The PG branch's `params: list = []` is now dead code but harmless (`conn.fetch(sql, *params)` with empty params is safe).
- The `slug`/`resolve_slug(resort_hint)` variable is no longer used here (comment notes other functions still use it) — no injection or bypass.

**Authorization / tenant isolation**:
- lyai-ski is single-tenant (Portes du Soleil domain). The `/api/alerts` endpoint already exposes all alerts to all users — the chat's per-station recorte was a UX filter, not an authz boundary. The change explicitly aligns chat with the screen. No confidentiality regression, no cross-tenant leak (there are no tenants).

**Phase 2c checks**:
- No new sink args, no allowlists, no observability sinks touched, no fail-open state drift (the removed guard was not a security guard — it was a query narrowing that produced false-negative user-facing text).
- SQL: `where` is a hardcoded string; f-string interpolates only a literal. No SQL injection.
- Mongo: no operator-shape injection possible; query is a static literal.

**Correctness/behavior note (not a security finding)**: `params: list = []` and the `*params` unpack are now dead code; the `f"""..."""` sql string no longer needs to be an f-string. Cosmetic only.

No security vulnerabilities introduced by this change.

@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+"""IP -> pais ISO2, sin dependencias y sin llamadas externas.
+
+Lee backend/data/geoip_paises.tsv (lo construye scripts/geoip-construir-tabla.py desde los
+ficheros publicos de los 5 RIR). Se carga UNA vez, perezosamente, en dos listas paralelas y
+se busca por biseccion: 261.020 rangos son ~4 MB de RAM y ~1 microsegundo por consulta.
+
+No guarda la IP en ningun sitio: recibe la cadena, devuelve dos letras y olvida.
+Si la tabla no existe, devuelve None y quien llame decide — nunca revienta.
+"""
+import bisect
+import os
+from typing import Optional
+
+_TABLA = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
+                      'data', 'geoip_paises.tsv')
+_inicios: list = []
+_fines: list = []
+_paises: list = []
+_cargada = False
+
+
+def _carga() -> None:
+    global _cargada
+    if _cargada:
+        return
+    _cargada = True                       # aunque falle: no reintentar en cada peticion
+    try:
+        with open(_TABLA, 'r', encoding='ascii') as f:
+            for linea in f:
+                a, b, cc = linea.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
+                _inicios.append(int(a))
+                _fines.append(int(b))
+                _paises.append(cc)
+    except Exception:
+        _inicios.clear(); _fines.clear(); _paises.clear()
+
+
+def pais(ip: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
+    """'178.63.165.87' -> 'DE'. None si no es IPv4, no esta en la tabla, o no hay tabla.
+
+    IPv6 devuelve None a proposito: los RIR lo publican en otro formato y en este dominio
+    la inmensa mayoria del trafico movil llega por IPv4. Mejor None honesto que un pais
+    inventado."""
+    if not ip:
+        return None
+    _carga()
+    if not _inicios:
+        return None
+    try:
+        a, b, c, d = (int(x) for x in ip.strip().split('.'))
+        if not all(0 <= v <= 255 for v in (a, b, c, d)):
+            return None
+        n = (a << 24) | (b << 16) | (c << 8) | d
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    i = bisect.bisect_right(_inicios, n) - 1
+    if i < 0 or n > _fines[i]:
+        return None
+    return _paises[i]


=== DIFF: scripts/geoip-construir-tabla.py ===
@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Construye la tabla IP→pais del backend a partir de los ficheros publicos de los 5 RIR.
+
+Por que asi y no con MaxMind: GeoLite2 es gratis pero exige CUENTA y CLAVE DE LICENCIA, o sea
+un secreto mas que rotar y un tercero del que depender. Los `delegated-*-latest` de los RIR son
+publicos, sin cuenta, sin clave, y son la fuente de la que MaxMind tambien bebe para el pais.
+
+Salida: backend/data/geoip_paises.tsv  (inicio_int  fin_int  ISO2), ordenada por inicio.
+Uso:    python3 scripts/geoip-construir-tabla.py
+Cron:   una vez al mes basta; los rangos por pais se mueven muy despacio.
+"""
+import io, os, sys, urllib.request
+
+RIR = {
+    'ripencc':  'https://ftp.ripe.net/pub/stats/ripencc/delegated-ripencc-latest',
+    'arin':     'https://ftp.arin.net/pub/stats/arin/delegated-arin-extended-latest',
+    'apnic':    'https://ftp.apnic.net/stats/apnic/delegated-apnic-latest',
+    'lacnic':   'https://ftp.lacnic.net/pub/stats/lacnic/delegated-lacnic-latest',
+    'afrinic':  'https://ftp.afrinic.net/pub/stats/afrinic/delegated-afrinic-latest',
+}
+RAIZ = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+DESTINO = os.path.join(RAIZ, 'backend', 'data', 'geoip_paises.tsv')
+
+
+def ip2int(s):
+    a, b, c, d = (int(x) for x in s.split('.'))
+    return (a << 24) | (b << 16) | (c << 8) | d
+
+
+def main():
+    rangos = []
+    for nombre, url in RIR.items():
+        try:
+            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r:
+                texto = r.read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')
+        except Exception as e:
+            print('  ✗ %-9s %s' % (nombre, e), file=sys.stderr)
+            continue
+        n = 0
+        for linea in texto.splitlines():
+            p = linea.split('|')
+            # rir|CC|ipv4|inicio|cuantas|fecha|estado
+            if len(p) < 7 or p[2] != 'ipv4' or len(p[1]) != 2:
+                continue
+            if p[6] not in ('allocated', 'assigned'):
+                continue
+            try:
+                ini = ip2int(p[3]); cuantas = int(p[4])
+            except Exception:
+                continue
+            if cuantas <= 0:
+                continue
+            rangos.append((ini, ini + cuantas - 1, p[1]))
+            n += 1
+        print('  ✓ %-9s %6d rangos' % (nombre, n))
+
+    if len(rangos) < 50000:
+        print('🔴 ABORTADO · solo %d rangos, algo ha fallado. NO se toca la tabla buena.' % len(rangos),
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    rangos.sort()
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(DESTINO), exist_ok=True)
+    tmp = DESTINO + '.tmp'
+    with io.open(tmp, 'w', encoding='ascii') as f:
+        for ini, fin, cc in rangos:
+            f.write('%d\t%d\t%s\n' % (ini, fin, cc))
+    os.replace(tmp, DESTINO)   # atomico: nadie lee una tabla a medio escribir
+    print('\n✅ %s · %d rangos · %.1f MB' % (DESTINO, len(rangos), os.path.getsize(DESTINO) / 1048576))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())

### **Claude** `01:12`

Based on my review of the three touched files:

**Data flow trace (server.py telemetry_screen)**: `X-Forwarded-For` → first comma-split value → `geoip_pais(ip)` → whitelisted through `_PAISES_OK` (8 countries + "otro" + "nd") → Prometheus label. No shell/SQL/eval/FS sinks are reached; the value only becomes a Prometheus label constrained by a hard whitelist.

**Cardinality (Phase 2c)**: Whitelist (`_PAISES_OK`) closed at 8 country codes plus "otro"/"nd" fallbacks — no cardinality explosion possible even if an attacker spoofs XFF.

**IP parsing (geoip.py)**: Bounded (`0 <= v <= 255`), rejects malformed/IPv6 by returning None. `_carga()` catches all exceptions and returns None from `pais()`; only invoked from an `async def` handler so no true thread race on the lazy-init lists.

**XFF trust**: The `_xff.split(",")[0]` pattern matches the pre-existing `_rl_key` at server.py:4563, so it's the codebase's established convention (Traefik-fronted per infra comments). Not newly introduced by this diff, and impact is bounded by the whitelist.

**Build script (geoip-construir-tabla.py)**: HTTPS URLs hardcoded, no cert-verify override, strict `|`-field parsing, 50k-row threshold before overwrite, atomic `os.replace`. Downloaded content is written as parsed integers (no shell/eval), so a compromised RIR mirror can at most yield wrong-country lookups, not code execution.

### **Claude** `01:14`

I've read the docker-compose.yml and the new nginx config file that's being mounted. Let me analyze what this diff actually introduces.

**The change**: A `default.conf` is now mounted read-only into `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` in the `dev-ski-frontend` (nginx:alpine) container. The comment explains this is defensive — the config previously lived only inside the container and would be lost on `--force-recreate`.

**Security analysis of the mounted config**:

1. **Static-only serve, no upload/exec sinks** — root is `/var/www/dev.lyai.pro` mounted `:ro`, no PHP/proxy_pass/exec, no user-writable location. No SSRF, RCE, or injection surface.
2. **`try_files $uri $uri.html $uri/index.html /app/index.html`** — nginx normalizes `$uri` before matching (resolves `..`), so no path traversal. `.html` extension lookup is intended SPA behavior for pre-rendered pages.
3. **`location = /` → 302 `/app/`** — relative redirect, no open-redirect risk (no `$host`/`$scheme` in redirect target).
4. **`.apk` regex `\.apk$`** — sets MIME + `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="lyai-ski.apk"`. Root is populated by CI, not uploads, so no attacker-controlled file placement.
5. **`Cache-Control: public, immutable` on `/app/_expo/` and `/app/assets/`** — content-hashed filenames as documented; no sensitive content under these paths.
6. **Mount is `:ro`** — container cannot rewrite the config back into the repo.
7. **No new port exposure** — `8089:80` and Traefik networking pre-exist this diff.
8. **No new secrets, credentials, or env vars introduced**.

The diff is a preservation/defensive move (config-as-code) that eliminates silent drift on recreate. It does not introduce any new source→sink path, missing auth check, parser differential, over-broad grant, or fail-open state.

### **Claude** `05:13`

Analysis complete.

**Backend change (`calc_pds.py:836-840`)**: Inside `network_geojson()`, when the edge is a lift and the destination node's elevation is lower than the source's, `geom = geom[::-1]` creates a NEW reversed list bound to the local `geom` — the original list in the cached graph edges (`_load()` result) is not mutated, so the `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` state is safe. The reversed geometry only ends up in the fresh GeoJSON features. Coordinates come from a trusted internal graph, not user input; no injection surface. The consumer (`network_geojson_live()` served by the API) receives a well-formed FeatureCollection.

**Frontend change (`banco-mapa/webroot/index.html`)**: adds pattern/arrow style controls to an internal dev tool. All values feed `setPaintProperty`/`setLayoutProperty` on MapLibre with numeric/enum/hex-color values coerced via `+value` or read from constrained `<select>`/`<range>` inputs. `_dash()` correctly returns `null` (not `[]`) to clear a dasharray. The new symbol layer uses a static `text-field:'>'` — no user-controlled string reaches the map style. No XSS/SSRF/injection surface introduced.

Neither change adds an entry point, sink, or trust boundary crossing. No parser differentials, no allowlist edits, no gate/action mismatches, no fail-open paths.

### **Claude** `05:48`

This is a local dev/testing tool ("banco del mapa" = map bench) marked `noindex,nofollow` with all state driven by DOM controls and localStorage on the same origin. Reviewing the changes:

1. New CSS `.subt` — presentation only.
2. New DOM inputs `kCasL`, `cCasL`, `nFle` — read via `chk()`, `.value`, and `+…||default`. `nFle` comes from a `<select>` with options 1–6; the `+o.nFle||3` fallback in `_derivado` is only fed by the same-origin `localStorage`/preset state produced by the same page.
3. `new Array(Math.max(1, v.nFle) + 1).join('>')` — the value flows into MapLibre's `text-field` layout property, not HTML, so there is no XSS. In principle a maliciously edited localStorage entry with a giant integer could cause a large string alloc, but (a) that requires attacker-controlled same-origin access (already game over), (b) this is a local, `noindex,nofollow` dev bench, not a production surface, and (c) the diff didn't remove any pre-existing cap.
4. All other diff lines are label renames, splitting one contour control into piste/lift pairs, and a build-timestamp string update — no sinks touched.

No source→sink path introduces new attacker-controllable data reaching a dangerous sink.

Based on the diff review:

**tools/banco-mapa/webroot/index.html:**
- The new `_pintaLista` code uses `innerHTML` with `g.hora`, `g.resumen`, and `g.motivo` values retrieved from `localStorage`. Tracing sources:
  - `g.hora` = `new Date().toTimeString().slice(0,5)` — hardcoded shape
  - `g.resumen` comes from `_resumen(a)` which concatenates only hardcoded input-element IDs found in `document.querySelectorAll(SEL_MANDOS)` — no user input
  - `g.motivo` is set from hardcoded literals (`'antes de aplicar '+g.hora`, `'borrado '+m.hora`) — no user input
  - The `<pre>` detail element uses `.textContent`, which is safe
- The `<details>` change for `panA` and the CSS grid columns change are pure layout with no data flow
- The PIN is explicitly documented as UX friction, not security ("está en claro, y el banco es tu navegador"), and the tool is a developer tool at dev.lyai.pro/banco-mapa

**frontend/src/components/RouteMap3D.tsx:**
- The new `h-lift-dir` symbol layer uses a hardcoded `text-field: '>>>'`, hardcoded filter, hardcoded paint properties. No attacker-influenceable values reach the layer definition
- The claim about backend-guaranteed direction orientation is a rendering/UX correctness matter, not a security boundary

No source→sink path for injection, no auth/authorization logic, no new entry points, and no removal of a security control. Sibling handlers (other `add({...})` calls) all use the same static-config pattern with no differential to flag.

### **Claude** `06:16`

I've analyzed the diff and its full context.

**Summary of the change:** The diff adds a `borrador` variable to preserve typed textarea content across the 3-second poll-and-repaint cycle. It also adds a `refrescaCabecera()` helper and an input event listener.

**Security trace:**

1. **`borrador` source → sink**: The only writer is the input event handler which does `borrador = e.target.value` when `e.target.id === 'ag-txt'`. The textarea is created only by `pinta()` itself inside `raiz`. So `borrador` is strictly the user's own typed text in their own browser session — no cross-user vector.

2. **XSS in the new textarea interpolation** (`'...>' + esc(borrador) + '</textarea>'`): The `esc()` function escapes `&`, `<`, `>`. Inside a `<textarea>` (RCDATA context), the only way to break out is via `</textarea>`; since `<` is escaped to `&lt;`, breakout is prevented. Safe.

3. **`refrescaCabecera()`**: Uses `textContent` (not innerHTML) for `.ag-quien` and `.ag-cuando`, and sets `.ag-luz` className from `nivel()` which returns a controlled string in `{'on','idle','off'}`. Safe.

4. **Reset on submit/cancel/copy**: `borrador = ''` — no security implication.

5. **Fetch/send path unchanged**: `envia()` still reads `t.value` (the live textarea) — not `borrador` — and posts to `api/pedido`. No new sink.

6. **Input listener scoping**: `raiz.addEventListener('input', ...)` is scoped to the panel root; only elements the panel itself renders can hit `id === 'ag-txt'`.

No new entry points, no new sinks, no new data flows to logs/exec/SQL/HTML-parse contexts, no gate changes. The change is a pure client-side UX fix (preserving textarea state across a repaint) with proper HTML-escaping applied to the interpolated draft text.

### **Claude** `06:42`

Based on my analysis of the diff, let me trace the data flows:

**agente.py changes:**
- `--responder`: CLI-controlled text → stored in JSON `hilo` (`{"de": "claude", "h": HH:MM, "txt": a.responder}`)
- `--cola` block: reads queue JSON files → copies `texto`/`selector` fields into `hilo` as `{"de": "ignacio", "h": ..., "txt": ..., "ancla": ...}`

**build_web.py changes:**
- CSS + JS rewrite of the side panel
- New `hilo` (thread) rendering that reads `estado-agente.json` every 3s

**Sinks I traced:**
1. **XSS via `innerHTML` in `pintaHilo()`**: Every variable interpolated (`estado.sesion`, `m.h`, `m.ancla`, `m.txt`) is wrapped in `esc()` which escapes `&`, `<`, `>`. All escaped values are placed between tags, not inside attributes, so quote-escaping isn't needed. The only unescaped class token (`'yo' / 'el'`) is a hard-coded ternary, not attacker-influenced.
2. **`monta()` static template**: no interpolation.
3. **`esc()` of ancla/txt from queue → JSON → browser**: even if `api/pedido` writer accepted arbitrary payloads, browser rendering is safe.
4. **File writes in `agente.py`**: `guardar()` writes to fixed `FICHERO` path via `os.replace` (atomic). `shutil.move` uses `os.path.basename(f)` so filename traversal in queue names can't escape `cola/atendidos/`.
5. **Dedup key `(h, txt)`**: Both fields are strings on the write paths in this diff; no injection into a downstream sink.
6. **`--responder` text**: CLI-local, operator-supplied; stored, then escaped in browser.
7. **`estado-agente.json` now containing chat**: file is written 0o644 into the webroot, but per project memory the site is behind auth ("sitio interno … contraseña"), and the pre-existing `acciones` field already carried free-text under the same permissions — not a regression from this diff.
8. **`MAX_HILO=40` cap**: bounds message count (not per-message size), but no attacker-controlled writer to `hilo` is introduced by this diff — the still-unimplemented `api/pedido` endpoint is what would matter for that.

I don't find a source→sink path with insufficient mitigation in the changed files.

### SEC-016 [warn]

### SEC-019+SEC-020 [warn]
PARCIAL: litellm retirado de requirements.txt (dep muerta, commit 0293a49). PENDIENTE: upgrade Traefik v2.10->fixed (CVE-2026-25949) — BLOQUEADO en Ignacio (ventana de downtime del ingress). Sigue OPEN.
### SEC-021 [alert]
n8n: Google API keys hardcodeadas en workflows. En lyai_db (public.workflow_entity, 37 workflows) hay 9 workflows con Google API key hardcodeada en el JSON de nodos (PLAINTEXT), 1 ACTIVO: id QKdQtKzHPj0lKsOo 'Workflow LyAi Corregido' (AIzaSyAI...). Los 8 restantes inactivos (AIzaSyAV.../AIzaSyDE...). Plaintext en la BD = tambien en todo dump/backup de lyai_db. n8n corre en lyai.pro. FIX: mover las keys al credential store cifrado de n8n (usa N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY, no node params); ROTAR las keys expuestas en Google Cloud; borrar/rehacer los 8 workflows muertos. Nota: el brief decia 8; verificados 9 con key (1 activo).
### SEC-022 [alert]
WORKER_PIN debil. server.py:2114 WORKER_PIN=os.environ.get('WORKER_PIN','1500'); valor en .env tambien 4 digitos. Protege DELETE /alerts/{id}, /admin/chat/analytics y escrituras de alerts con '!=' (no constant-time) y SIN throttle -> 10^4 fuerza bruta. Default '1500' commiteado en source (recuperable via SEC-014). FIX: PIN largo/aleatorio o token; rate-limit + lockout; comparacion con hmac.compare_digest.
### SEC-023 [alert]
GDPR/nFADP: sin base legal ni transparencia (audiencia FR+CH). Francia (GDPR) + Suiza (nFADP). La app almacena PII: historial de chat (texto libre), push tokens, contact address de OTP (email/telefono), posts de feed, session tokens. NO hay politica de privacidad, base legal/consentimiento, ni retencion documentada (grep privacy|gdpr|rgpd|consent|retention = 0 en codigo). Sin TTL en historial de chat. Ademas el flujo OTP es scaffold in-memory sin entrega real de email/SMS (server.py:7806 'delivery NOT implemented') -> 2FA no funcional. FIX: aviso de privacidad (Art.13 GDPR / nFADP) enlazado en la app; politica de retencion + TTL en chat/logs; registro de actividades de tratamiento; base legal explicita; completar o retirar el flujo OTP. ESCALAR a Ignacio: decision legal, no solo tecnica.

### **Claude** `08:05`

Reading the changed section carefully:

**Data flow analysis of `pintaHilo` (the main new logic):**

The dangerous-looking part is the markdown post-processing on `m.txt`:
```js
var cuerpo = esc(m.txt || '');
cuerpo = cuerpo.replace(/^(\s*)(⏺|●)\s*(\w+)\(([^)]*)\)/gm,
  '$1<span class="ag-tool">⏺ <i>$3</i>($4)</span>');
cuerpo = cuerpo.replace(/\*\*([^*\\n]+)\*\*/g, '<b>$1</b>')
               .replace(/`([^`\\n]+)`/g, '<span class="ag-cod">$1</span>');
return '<p class="ag-yo">' + cuerpo + '</p>';
```

Checking `esc()` at lines 1051-1054: escapes `&`, `<`, `>`. That's sufficient because the substituted output lands in **text positions** only — never in an attribute value where unquoted quotes would matter.

Tracing each regex capture:
- `$3` = `\w+` (word chars) → safe as `<i>` content.
- `$4` = `[^)]*` — post-escape, so any injected `<script>` is already `&lt;script&gt;`; it renders as literal text inside the span, not markup.
- `**X**` and `` `X` `` bodies come from already-escaped content — no re-injection.

The comment even calls it out: "SIEMPRE sobre texto ya escapado, nunca al reves." The ordering is correct.

**Other new sinks:**
- `m.ancla` — wrapped in `esc()` ✓
- `estado.pendientes` — used as `col.textContent = 'cola: ' + p` ✓
- New `<div class="ag-estado">` — static HTML, no interpolation ✓
- Ctrl+Enter handler — no data flow to sink ✓

**Regex DoS check:** The three new regexes are all linear (content classes exclude the delimiter or use `\w+`); no catastrophic backtracking.

**Pre-existing `pintaAdj` `<img src="' + a.url` uses `URL.createObjectURL()` locally** — not attacker-controllable and not in this diff.

No security vulnerabilities introduced by this change.

### **Claude** `08:06`

I've read the changed section and its surrounding context. This diff modifies `_instantanea` (a client-side history-dedup helper in an internal banco-mapa tool):

- Before: only compared current state against the newest saved entry.
- After: searches the whole list; if the state already exists at index > 0, splices it out, refreshes its `hora` timestamp, and unshifts it to the top.

Data-flow check:
- Sources: `_leeAjustes()` (local settings) and `_guardados()` (list previously persisted by this same code).
- Sinks: `_escribe(l)` → `_sube(l)` (POSTs the list to `/api/banco/ajustes`) and `_pintaLista()` (renders history rows).
- The moved entry `g` is an already-existing item from the same list — no new tainted field enters the pipeline. `hora` is generated from `new Date().toTimeString().slice(0,5)`, not attacker-controlled.
- `_pintaLista` uses `innerHTML` with `g.resumen`/`g.motivo`, but those come from prior stored entries (unchanged by this diff), not from anything the + lines introduce; the reordering doesn't add a new source.
- The other + line only updates a static build-time string ("banco montado el 2026-08-30 08:05") in the provenance banner.

No new entry point, no new sink, no new data-flow, no change to auth/PIN gating (the PIN prompt at line 1642 is untouched). The "cap" `_recorta` still runs via `_escribe`. Nothing security-relevant regresses.

### **Claude** `08:10`

Looking at this diff, it's changes to a static HTML file (`banco-mapa/webroot/index.html`) — an internal map-tuning development tool ("banco-mapa"). The changes add a new "Acotado del mapa" UI panel with three controls (a checkbox and two range sliders) whose values feed into MapLibre's `setMaxBounds()` and `setMinZoom()` methods, plus a serialization tweak in `_derivado()` and a timestamp bump in the provenance text.

- `zMin` — `<input type="range" min="60" max="130">` → `num()/10` → `m.setMinZoom()`

All three values are:
- Same-origin, user-controlled by the operator of the tool himself (no cross-principal exposure)
- Constrained to numeric ranges by HTML controls and coerced through `num()`/`chk()`/`+` numeric coercion
- Consumed only by client-side MapLibre configuration APIs — no shell/SQL/eval/HTML sinks, no filesystem, no outbound HTTP, no auth boundary
- The `_derivado()` serialization stores them into a settings object with no downstream dangerous consumer visible

The updated line 1871 only modifies a static provenance string with a bumped timestamp; no user data is interpolated.

There is no attacker-controllable path to any dangerous sink introduced by this diff. This is a purely UI-facing map-viewport constraint feature in an internal dev tool.

=== DIFF: tools/calc2/normaliza_nombres.py ===
@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Normaliza las MAYUSCULAS de los nombres del grafo (pistas, remontes, enlaces).
+
+Por que (Ignacio, 2026-08-30): «en los nombres de los bares, pistas, etc, no respetas las
+mayusculas». Medido: de los 3.334 nombres con dato, 1.654 (el 50 %) vienen ENTEROS en
+mayusculas y solo un 32 % trae minusculas. `TK du Poireau 1` convive con `TK DU LAC`. Es
+inconsistencia del ORIGEN, no del mapa — por eso se arregla en el dato y no al pintar: asi el
+mapa, el chat y el calculador dicen lo mismo.
+
+QUE TOCA Y QUE NO
+  · Solo los nombres ENTERAMENTE en mayusculas. Los que ya traen minusculas se dejan: alguien
+    los escribio bien y no hay que adivinar.
+  · Las SIGLAS de remonte (TK, TS, TSD, TC...) se quedan como estan: son tipos de aparato.
+  · Las particulas francesas van en minuscula, menos si abren el nombre.
+  · Numeros y numeros romanos, intactos.
+
+Uso:
+    python3 normaliza_nombres.py            # ENSAYO: escribe nada, enseña que cambiaria
+    python3 normaliza_nombres.py --aplica   # escribe, con respaldo al lado
+"""
+import json, re, shutil, sys, datetime, pathlib
+
+GRAFO = pathlib.Path('/opt/lyai/app/lyai-ski/backend/data/calc2/graph_osm.json')
+SIGLAS = {'TK','TS','TSD','TSD6','TC','TCD','TPH','TSF','TS4','TS6','TK1','TK2','FUN','DMC','TMX'}
+# Dos familias, y la distincion la saco el ensayo del 30-08:
+#  · PREPOSICIONES: enlazan, van SIEMPRE en minuscula salvo que abran el nombre entero.
+#    «TK DU LAC» -> «TK du Lac», que es como se escribe en frances.
+#  · ARTICULOS: forman parte del topónimo. Tras la sigla del aparato ABREN el nombre y van en
+#    mayuscula — «TSD LES COMBES» es el telesilla de *Les Combes*, no de «les Combes».
+#    A mitad de nombre vuelven a minuscula: «TSD de Pré la Joux».
+PREPOSICIONES = {'de','du','des','d','et','sur','sous','aux','au','a','en','par'}
+ARTICULOS     = {'la','le','les','l'}
+PARTICULAS    = PREPOSICIONES | ARTICULOS
+
+def _es_sigla(t: str) -> bool:
+    """TK, TS, TSD, TC, TD6, TLC, TPH... — codigos de tipo de aparato.
+
+    El ensayo del 30-08 saco `TD6 CASES -> Td6 Cases` y `TLC SUPER -> Tlc Super`: la lista fija
+    no cubria todas. Un patron las coge todas y no hay que ir ampliandola cada vez que PdS
+    inventa un tipo."""
+    return bool(re.fullmatch(r'T[A-Z]{1,3}\d*', t)) or t in SIGLAS
+
+
+def _capitaliza(t: str) -> str:
+    """Respeta el guion: PETIT-CHÂTEL -> Petit-Châtel, no Petit-châtel (defecto del ensayo)."""
+    return '-'.join(x[:1].upper() + x[1:] for x in t.split('-'))
+
+
+def normaliza(n: str) -> str:
+    if not n or not n.isupper():        # ya trae minusculas o esta vacio: no se toca
+        return n
+    fuera = []
+    trozos = re.split(r'(\s+)', n)
+    tras_sigla = False                  # ¿la palabra anterior era una sigla de aparato?
+    for i, p in enumerate(trozos):
+        if not p.strip():
+            fuera.append(p); continue
+        base = p.strip("()[].,")
+        # La sigla del aparato solo puede ir AL PRINCIPIO. Sin esta condicion, «STADE TETE
+        # BOEUFS» salia «Stade TETE Boeufs»: TETE encaja por casualidad con el patron
+        # T+3 mayusculas. Quinto defecto que caza el ensayo en seco.
+        if (i == 0 and _es_sigla(base)) or base.isdigit():
+            fuera.append(p); tras_sigla = True; continue
+        if re.fullmatch(r'[IVXLC]+', base) and len(base) <= 4:   # numero romano
+            fuera.append(p); tras_sigla = False; continue
+        b = p.lower()
+        # Las particulas van en minuscula SALVO que abran el nombre — y tras una sigla de
+        # aparato el nombre EMPIEZA: «TSD LES COMBES» es el telesilla de *Les Combes*, no
+        # «les Combes». Ese matiz salio del ensayo, no de suponerlo.
+        primera = (i == 0) or tras_sigla
+        limpio = b.strip("()[].,\'")
+        # una preposicion nunca abre nombre salvo que sea LA primera palabra de todo
+        if i > 0 and limpio in PREPOSICIONES:
+            fuera.append(b); tras_sigla = False; continue
+        if not primera and limpio in ARTICULOS:
+            fuera.append(b); tras_sigla = False; continue
+        if "'" in b:
+            izq, _, der = b.partition("'")
+            fuera.append((izq if not primera and izq in PARTICULAS else _capitaliza(izq)) + "'" + _capitaliza(der))

+        fuera.append(_capitaliza(b)); tras_sigla = False
+    return ''.join(fuera)

+def main():
+    aplica = '--aplica' in sys.argv
+    g = json.loads(GRAFO.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
+    cambios = []
+    for e in g['edges']:
+        n = e.get('name') or ''
+        m = normaliza(n)
+        if m != n:
+            cambios.append((n, m))
+            if aplica:

+            vistos.add(a); muestra.append((a, b))
+    print("nombres distintos afectados: %d\n" % len(muestra))

+    if not aplica:
+        print("\nENSAYO · no se ha escrito nada. Con --aplica se escribe (y se respalda antes).")
+        return 0
+    resp = GRAFO.with_suffix('.json.bak-%s' % datetime.datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M'))
+    shutil.copy2(GRAFO, resp)
+    tmp = GRAFO.with_suffix('.json.tmp')
+    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(g, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
+    tmp.replace(GRAFO)
+    print("\n✅ escrito · respaldo en %s" % resp.name)
+    return 0
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    sys.exit(main())

I've read both changed files in full. Let me assess:

**tools/calc2/normaliza_nombres.py** — an offline CLI script that:
- Reads a hard-coded absolute path (`/opt/lyai/app/lyai-ski/backend/data/calc2/graph_osm.json`) — no attacker-controlled path.
- Parses trusted JSON, applies pure-Python string capitalization heuristics via `re.split` / `str.lower` / `str.strip`.
- Writes back via `tmp.write_text(json.dumps(...))` + `tmp.replace(GRAFO)` and takes a `shutil.copy2` backup.
- No `subprocess`, no `eval`, no `os.system`, no path from argv/env, no network, no SQL, no HTML.
- The `--aplica` flag is a simple `in sys.argv` boolean.

No source→sink chain. Backup filename includes only a `strftime` timestamp (no user input). Nothing to flag.

**tools/banco-mapa/webroot/index.html** — an internal design/tuning "banco" page (per memory: `dev.lyai.pro/banco-mapa`, non-production, dev-only tuning). The + lines:
- Add DOM controls (`<input type=checkbox|color|range>`, `<select>` with fixed literal options `/`, `X`, `\\`).
- Add two MapLibre symbol layers using `m.addLayer({..., layout:{'text-field': '/', 'symbol-placement':'line', ...}})` — fixed string literals in the initial layer definition.
- Feed values into `_lay(m,'h-off-obra','text-field', v.gObra)` / `_pin(m,'h-off-stop','text-color', v.cStop)` — MapLibre's `setLayoutProperty`/`setPaintProperty` render to WebGL/canvas, not to HTML; these are not XSS sinks. `symbol-spacing` and `dObra`/`dStop` are numeric (through `num()`).
- The `paletaR` change handler does `PALETAS[this.value]` (own property lookup on a local object) and assigns to fixed `<input type=color>` `.value` fields. `this.value` comes from the fixed select options; `.value` on a color input is coerced to a `#rrggbb` string. No sink.
- `_colorDifRuta()` builds a MapLibre `match` expression from color-input values — same story.
- No `innerHTML`, no `eval`, no `new Function`, no template-injection, no network I/O added.

No attacker-influenceable source reaches a sensitive sink in either file.

### **Claude** `08:37`

I've read every touched region of the changed file in full and traced each new construct:

**New/modified pieces reviewed:**

1. **CSS block (lines ~961–1015)** — purely visual (colors, borders, spacing, layout). No sink.

2. **`monta()` innerHTML (lines 1137–1162)** — the assigned HTML is a static string literal with no interpolation of any external value. Not an XSS surface.

3. **`refresca()` (lines 1189–1196)** — updates `.ag-env.disabled` (boolean) and `.ag-modo .cola` via `.textContent`. `estado.pendientes` reaches `.textContent`, which is XSS-safe. No new sink.

4. **`ponAncla()` (lines 1245–1256)** — parses `elegido.sel` (a CSS-path string built locally in the user's own browser by walking the DOM the user clicked on) with regexes, then writes the result via `.textContent`. Even if the DOM contained hostile text, `.textContent` neutralizes any HTML meaning. No injection possible; no server-side sink involved.

5. **`pintaGrabar()` new lines (1339–1340)** — toggles a CSS class based on a local boolean. No sink.

6. **`envia()` (line 1392)** — added a bare `ajustaAlto()` call after successful send; purely cosmetic (resets the textarea's rendered height). No effect on the request itself.

7. **`ajustaAlto()` + focusin/focusout handlers (lines 1457–1475)** — read `scrollHeight`, set `style.height`, toggle a class. No sinks, no data flow to network/storage/exec.

**No entry-point/sink pair is introduced or altered by this diff.** The endpoints called (`api/adjunto`, `api/pedido`) are unchanged; validation semantics (upload size cap, MIME filter, ctrl+Enter behavior, clipboard fallback) are unchanged. There's no logging, no dynamic code eval, no shell/SQL/path work, no permission/allowlist change, no parser differential, and no server-side change at all — this is client-side chrome for a UI panel.

### **Claude** `09:28`

The diff only adds client-side UI controls (checkboxes, color pickers, range sliders, a font `<select>`) to a local dev tool (`banco-mapa`, a MapLibre style-tuning bench) and wires those DOM values into MapLibre's `setPaintProperty` / `setLayoutProperty` via the existing `_pin`/`_lay`/`_ver` helpers.

Trace:
- Sources: `document.getElementById(id).value` / `.checked` on inputs the operator fills in themselves (color picker → validated `#RRGGBB`, range → numeric coerced with `+`, select → bounded to hardcoded options, checkbox → boolean).
- Sinks: MapLibre paint/layout properties on `stn-lbl` and `stn-dot` layers. No shell, SQL, HTML render, filesystem, network, auth, or logging sink is introduced.
- No new HTTP endpoint, no new fetch, no new eval/Function, no innerHTML. The only outbound HTTP is the pre-existing `fetch('setup.js',{method:'HEAD'})` (unchanged behavior — only the version string got a new timestamp).
- The additions to `_derivado` just add the same keys to the serialized state used for save/restore — no new sink there either.

There is no attacker-influenceable path to a security-relevant sink in this change.

### **Claude** `09:38`

The diff is a pure presentational change: it swaps rare/emoji-dependent Unicode glyphs (⌖, 🛡, ⏺, ＋) for inline SVG icons rendered from a static `ICO` map built at module load. There are no new sources, no new sinks, and no attacker-influenced value flows into the added code.

Verification:
- `svg(d, relleno)` is only ever called with hardcoded path/circle strings from the `ICO` literal — no user input reaches the SVG string, and no attribute value is interpolated from a dynamic source.
- The added `ICO.mira` inserted into `innerHTML` at line 1244 sits next to `esc(m.ancla)`; `esc` (line 1072–1075) still handles `&`, `<`, `>` on the dynamic value, and the SVG is a constant. Prepending a constant HTML string to a properly-escaped payload does not weaken the escape.
- Line 1276 (`caja.querySelector('span').textContent = '' + …`) uses `.textContent`, which remains safe regardless of the removed `⌖ ` prefix.
- Line 1249's regex character swap (`⏺|●`) and the `'$1<span class="ag-tool">● <i>$3</i>($4)</span>'` replacement still operate on already-`esc()`'d text (`cuerpo = esc(m.txt || '')` on line 1247), so it cannot introduce injection.
- No changes to routing, authz, filesystem, subprocess, network, deserialization, logging of sensitive data, or IaC.

### **Claude** `09:44`

The diff is a purely client-side UX change to the send-button state in the in-page agent panel:

- Adds a boolean `nadie` variable.
- Extracts the disable logic into `refrescaEnvio()`, which reads `t.value.trim()` and `adjuntos.length` only for truthiness, sets `env.disabled` to a boolean, and sets `env.title` to one of three static Spanish strings.
- Invokes `refrescaEnvio()` from existing places (attach, remove, send, input).

No new sinks are introduced: no `innerHTML`, no shell/exec/SQL/URL/path/fetch calls take user-controlled data as a result of these changes. The three `title` values are string literals. All new reads of `t.value` and `adjuntos` are boolean coercions. No cross-file callers rely on new behavior in a security-relevant way (button-disabled is a UX signal — the diff's own comment notes the send still falls back to the clipboard).

No parser/validator differentials, no gate/action mismatches, no observability leakage (`title` is set to constants), no allowlist/permission changes, no state-drift regressions.

### **Claude** `09:57`

Based on my review of the diff and the surrounding code:

**All changes are cosmetic/UI or a performance refactor with no security-relevant surface:**

1. **`theme.ts`** — Constant color palette changes only (no logic).

2. **`AlertMap3D.tsx` / `RouteMap3D.tsx`** — Color hex updates in `_difDeColor()` lookup tables and paint properties; hillshade/terrain exaggeration numeric tweaks; new `h-lift-dir` symbol layer using a fixed literal string `'>>>'`. None of these interpolate attacker-influenced data into new sinks. The HTML/JS template mechanism (`buildHtml`, `JSON.stringify(D)` into a `<script>` block) was not modified by this diff — the color and arrow changes are inside the pre-existing SETUP_JS string, and only literal constants change.

3. **`index.tsx`** — The eager 1×1 hidden `<Image>` preload is replaced with an idle-time `new window.Image(); img.src = uri` loop. Every URI in that loop resolves from a `require(...)` of a bundled asset (`POSTER_FORFAITS_NAVETTES_BY_LANG`, `WATERMARK_SELECTOR`, `SILUETA_TSDC6`) — all module-level, no user input. `_uriDe` never sees network- or user-derived data.

No new entry points, sinks, auth checks, allowlists, control-flow guards, IPC handlers, or observability writes are introduced. No parser/validator changes. No sibling-path parity issues. No registry fan-out impact (the color-code map in `_difDeColor` was updated consistently in both map components alongside `theme.ts`; the produced value flows into a fixed i18n dictionary lookup, not a sink).

### **Claude** `09:57`

I've read the full changed file. This is a local build script (`extraer_envio.py`) that reads Markdown files from `outreach/correos/*.md` and writes plain-text `.txt` files to `outreach/ENVIO/`. There is no network activity, no attacker-influenceable input, no auth boundary, and the only "external inputs" are the local `.md` files under version control.

Reviewing the changes against the method's patterns:

- **Sibling-path gate parity (opt-out exemption)**: The new `sin_baja` set that exempts entries from the CNIL/UWG opt-out QA check is populated ONLY from filenames the script itself generates during the `FORMULARIOS` loop — the source list is a hardcoded whitelist (`[("06-formularios-DE.md", "DE")]`). The QA loop tests `f not in sin_baja`, not a filename heuristic, so a regular email file cannot accidentally land in the exempt set. The code and comment explicitly justify this design ("la lista es explicita, no una heuristica sobre el nombre del fichero, para que nadie se libre por accidente").
- **Filename collisions**: `nombre` includes the monotonic `total` counter, so form filenames cannot collide with prior email filenames (which would risk falsely exempting an email).
- **Parser differential (`RE_ASUNTO_F`)**: `^\*\*(?:Objet|...|Asunto)\b[^:]*:\*\*\s*(.+?)\s*$` — `[^:]*` cannot skip a colon and the trailing `:**` is anchored, so the only extra tokens accepted vs `RE_ASUNTO` are non-colon characters between the label and the terminator, which then feed only into local file writes.
- **`re.DOTALL` on bold-stripping**: Non-greedy with `.+?`; no catastrophic backtracking, no injection sink.
- **Path handling**: `SRC`/`OUT` are hardcoded, filenames sanitized via `slug()` to `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`. The pre-existing `os.remove` loop on `OUT` was not touched.
- **Output sinks**: `print` statements emit filenames and counts, not PII or credentials. Written `.txt` files are the intended product.
- **CI/CD, RBAC, LLM prompts, IPC, deserialization, shell/SQL/HTML sinks**: none present.

No security-relevant vulnerability introduced by this diff.

---

### **Claude** `09:57`

Based on my review of all four changed files:

**frontend/app/index.tsx** — The changes refactor image preloading from eager hidden `<Image>` elements to a deferred `requestIdleCallback`-based loop. The URIs come from static `require()` calls (bundler-resolved asset paths), not user input. `_precargaOciosa(language)` uses `language` only to filter which static key to skip, never as a URI source. `new Image(); img.src = uri` is a benign browser image fetch with no code-execution semantics.

**frontend/src/components/AlertMap3D.tsx** — Changes are cosmetic: hex color palette swaps for lift lines, updated hillshade exaggeration constant, and a new `h-lift-dir` MapLibre symbol layer with a **static** `text-field:'>>>'`. The `_difDeColor` dict updates the color→difficulty lookup keys to match the new palette — this is a pure lookup with no sink. `_esc` remains unchanged.

**frontend/src/components/RouteMap3D.tsx** — Same-shape cosmetic changes: color hex swaps in the `ski` layer `match` expression, terrain exaggeration bumped from 1.21 to 1.63, and the existing arrow symbol's text-size/spacing/color adjusted. All values are literals.

**frontend/src/utils/theme.ts** — Only hex-color constant reassignments (`pisteGreen/Blue/Red/Black`).

No new entry points, no new sinks, no attacker-controlled data reaching any sink, no auth/gate logic, no parser changes, no observability sinks receiving new fields, no allowlist edits, no IaC or CI changes. This is a visual-design change.

+def turnos_notebook(ruta):
+    """Parte el export de Gemini Notebook en turnos (quien, html, fuentes).
+
+    El export es HTML plano —p, ul, li, strong, em, code, pre, hr— sin scripts ni
+    recursos externos, asi que se puede incrustar tal cual. Lo unico que se toca
+    son los marcadores «[Source: N: fichero.pdf]», que van intercalados CADA POCAS
+    FRASES y hacen el texto ilegible: se retiran del cuerpo y se listan una vez por
+    turno, que es donde sirven para algo.
+    """
+    crudo = io.open(ruta, encoding="utf-8").read()
+    cuerpo = crudo.split("<body>", 1)[-1].split("</body>", 1)[0]
+    trozos = re.split(r'<h[1-3][^>]*>\s*(User|Model)\s*</h[1-3]>', cuerpo)
+    fuera = []
+    for i in range(1, len(trozos), 2):
+        quien, txt = trozos[i], trozos[i + 1]
+        fuentes = sorted(set(re.findall(r'\[Source:\s*\d+:\s*([^\]]+?)\s*\]', txt)))
+        txt = re.sub(r'\s*\[Source:\s*\d+:[^\]]*\]', '', txt)
+        txt = re.sub(r'^\s*<hr\s*/?>\s*', '', txt.strip())
+        txt = re.sub(r'\s*<hr\s*/?>\s*$', '', txt.strip())
+        if not re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', txt).strip():
+            continue
+        fuera.append((quien, txt.strip(), fuentes))
+    return fuera
+
+
+def pagina_notebook():
+    """La pagina del notebook: primero que fiabilidad tiene, luego lo aprovechable,
+    y al final la conversacion entera por si hay que comprobar cualquier cosa."""

+    pares = sum(1 for q, _, _ in t if q == "User")
+
+    def bloque(n, quien, html_txt, fuentes):

+        src = ""
+        if fuentes:
+            src = ('<p class="nb-fuentes"><span>Fuentes citadas:</span> '
+                   + " · ".join(html.escape(f) for f in fuentes) + "</p>")

+                f'<header><span class="nb-quien">{etiq}</span>'
+                f'<span class="nb-n">turno {n}</span></header>'
+                f'<div class="md">{html_txt}</div>{src}</article>')
+
+    hilo = "\n".join(bloque(i, q, h, f) for i, (q, h, f) in enumerate(t, 1))

+          comercios en 12 valles, 542.500 € en escenario moderado y 718.000 € en optimista.</p>

 JS = """
+/* ---- «Copiar la ficha»: la ficha en TEXTO PLANO, no en HTML ----------------
+   Una ficha son varias tablas. Copiar el HTML se pega bien en un editor rico y
+   fatal en el cuerpo de un correo o en una celda del seguimiento, que es donde
+   acaba. Asi que se reconstruye como texto: cabecera con nombre, pais y scores,
+   el enlace permanente a la ficha, y luego cada seccion con sus pares
+   etiqueta/valor. Se copia con navigator.clipboard, que exige HTTPS —lo hay— y
+   con respaldo por textarea, porque si la escritura falla y no se avisa, uno se
+   va a pegar creyendo que lleva la ficha encima.                              */
+(function () {
+  function textoDe(det) {
+    var out = [], nm = det.querySelector('summary .nm');
+    var meta = det.querySelector('summary .meta');
+    out.push((nm ? nm.textContent.trim() : det.id).toUpperCase());
+    /* Los «·» viven en <span class=dot> pegados a sus vecinos, asi que
+       textContent los devuelve como «88%·Austria·score 89.5». */
+    if (meta) out.push(meta.textContent.replace(/\\s*·\\s*/g, ' · ')
+                                       .replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim());
+    out.push(location.origin + location.pathname + '#' + det.id);
+    det.querySelectorAll('.org-b > h4, .org-b .scroll, .org-b ul').forEach(function (el) {
+      if (el.tagName === 'H4') { out.push('', el.textContent.trim().toUpperCase()); return; }
+      if (el.tagName === 'UL') {
+        el.querySelectorAll('li').forEach(function (li) {
+          out.push('  - ' + li.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim());
+        });
+        return;
+      }
+      el.querySelectorAll('tr').forEach(function (tr) {
+        var c = Array.prototype.map.call(tr.cells, function (td) {
+          return td.textContent.replace(/\\s+/g, ' ').trim();
+        }).filter(function (x) { return x; });
+        if (!c.length) return;
+        out.push(c.length === 2 ? '  ' + c[0] + ': ' + c[1] : '  ' + c.join(' · '));
+      });
+    });
+    return out.join('\\n').replace(/\\n{3,}/g, '\\n\\n').trim() + '\\n';
+  }
+
+  function avisa(btn, txt, mal) {
+    var antes = btn.textContent;
+    btn.textContent = txt;
+    btn.classList.toggle('mal', !!mal);
+    btn.classList.toggle('ok', !mal);
+    setTimeout(function () {
+      btn.textContent = antes; btn.classList.remove('ok', 'mal');
+    }, 2200);
+  }
+
+  function respaldo(txt, btn) {
+    try {
+      var ta = document.createElement('textarea');
+      ta.value = txt; ta.setAttribute('readonly', '');
+      ta.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:-9999px;top:0';
+      document.body.appendChild(ta); ta.select();
+      var ok = document.execCommand('copy');
+      document.body.removeChild(ta);
+      avisa(btn, ok ? 'Copiada ✓' : 'No se pudo copiar', !ok);
+    } catch (e) { avisa(btn, 'No se pudo copiar', true); }
+  }
+
+  document.addEventListener('click', function (ev) {
+    var btn = ev.target.closest && ev.target.closest('button[data-copiar]');
+    if (!btn) return;
+    ev.preventDefault();
+    ev.stopPropagation();          /* el boton vive dentro de un <details>:
+                                      sin esto el clic lo plegaria */
+    var det = document.getElementById(btn.getAttribute('data-copiar'));
+    if (!det) return avisa(btn, 'No se pudo copiar', true);
+    var txt = textoDe(det);
+    if (navigator.clipboard && navigator.clipboard.writeText) {
+      navigator.clipboard.writeText(txt).then(function () {
+        avisa(btn, 'Copiada ✓');
+      })['catch'](function () { respaldo(txt, btn); });
+    } else {
+      respaldo(txt, btn);
+    }
+  });
+})();

+<h1>European Ski Organizations Performance and Ranking Directory 2026 - Gemini Notebook</h1>
+<p>Exported on: 30/8/2026, 12:02:28 p.m.</p>
+<hr>
+<h3>User</h3>
+<p>si</p>
+<hr>
+<h3>Model</h3>
+<p>Arquitectura del Calculador de Rutas y Protocolo de Fallo de Datos (Intermaps API)</p>
+<p>Para garantizar la seguridad operacional y civil en dominios esquiables de alta montaña, el calculador de rutas de <strong>LyAi</strong> implementa una arquitectura de <strong>coexistencia tolerante a fallos</strong> [Source: 1: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] . Este sistema asume de forma defensiva que las conexiones de red en alta montaña son inestables y que las APIs de terceros (como <strong>Intermaps</strong>) pueden sufrir caídas, latencias o suministrar datos congelados (obsoletos) [Source: 2: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] .</p>
+<p>A continuación, se detalla el comportamiento lógico del calculador de rutas y el motor de alertas mediante un <strong>diagrama de flujo estructurado</strong> y su desglose técnico paso a paso.</p>
+<hr>
+<p>Diagrama de Flujo Técnico: Protocolo de Veto y Fallback</p>
+<pre><code>[ Inicio del Ciclo de Sincronización (Cada 120 segundos) ]
+                         │
+                         ▼
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐
+           │   Petición HTTPS GET a    │
+           │     Intermaps API         │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘
+                         │
+                         ├──────────────────────────────────────────┐
+                (¿Conexión Exitosa?)                                │ (Fallo de Red / Timeout)
+                         │ SI                                       │
+                         ▼                                          ▼
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐             ┌─────────────────────────────┐
+           │ Extraer Objeto JSON/XML y │             │ REGISTRO DE INCIDENCIA      │
+           │  leer metadato &#39;Timestamp&#39;│             │ Log en consola de auditoría │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘             └──────────────┬──────────────┘
+                         │                                          │
+                         ▼                                          │
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐                            │
+           │  Calcular Delta de Tiempo │                            │
+           │ Δt = T_actual - T_API     │                            │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘                            │
+                         │                                          │
+            (¿Δt es menor a 60 minutos?)                            │
+                         ├────────────────────────┐                 │
+                         │ SI                     │ NO              │
+                         ▼                        ▼                 ▼
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
+           │    ESTADO EN VERDE        │    │        ESTADO EN AMARILLO            │
+           │  (Sincronización Activa)  │    │  (Activación del Veto de Seguridad)  │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘    └──────────────────────┬───────────────┘
+                         │                                         │
+                         ▼                                         ▼
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
+           │ Mapear id_elemento con    │    │ Forzar Peso de Aristas = Infinito (∞)│
+           │ Grafo de OpenStreetMap    │    │ en el Grafo de Ruteo de la zona      │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘    └──────────────────────┬───────────────┘
+                         │                                         │
+                         ▼                                         ▼
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
+           │ Actualizar Grafo en App:  │    │ Recalcular Rutas Alternativas        │
+           │ Pistas Abiertas/Cerradas  │    │ evitando sectores afectados          │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘    └──────────────────────┬───────────────┘
+                         │                                         │
+                         ▼                                         ▼
+           ┌───────────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
+           │   Ruteo Estándar Activo   │    │ UI Front-End:                        │
+           │ (Cálculo normal de rutas) │    │ &quot;Estado de montaña en verificación&quot;  │
+           └─────────────┬─────────────┘    └──────────────────────┬───────────────┘
+                         │                                         │
+                         ▼                                         ▼
+                 [ Fin de Ciclo ]           ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
+                                            │ Mostrar botón con enlace directo al  │
+                                            │ Boletín Oficial de Pistas local      │
+                                            └──────────────────────┬───────────────┘
+                                                                   │
+                                                                   ▼
+                                                            [ Fin de Ciclo ]
+</code></pre>
+<hr>
+<p>Explicación Detallada del Proceso y Reglas de Negocio</p>
+<p>1. Ingesta y Mapeo en el Grafo de Ruteo</p>
+<p>El motor de ruteo de LyAi estructura el dominio esquiable mediante un grafo matemático compuesto por <strong>nodos</strong> (intersecciones de pistas, entradas y salidas de remontes) y <strong>aristas</strong> (el recorrido físico de las pistas y los trayectos de los remontes) [Source: 3: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] [Source: 4: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] .</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>Mapeo de Identificadores:</strong> Cada 120 segundos, la tarea programada (<em>cron job</em>) de LyAi realiza una llamada HTTPS a la API de Intermaps [Source: 2: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] . El sistema mapea el identificador dinámico de Intermaps (por ejemplo, <code>lift_104_status</code>) con la arista correspondiente en nuestro grafo de OpenStreetMap [Source: 3: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] [Source: 4: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] .-   <strong>Normalización:</strong> Si el estado es &quot;Abierto&quot; (estado binario <code>1</code>), el calculador mantiene la arista como transitable. Si es &quot;Cerrado&quot; (estado <code>0</code>), el peso de la arista se establece en infinito (<code>∞</code>), impidiendo que el algoritmo de Dijkstra o A* trace trayectos a través de ese tramo [Source: 1: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] [Source: 3: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>
+<p>2. Detección de Datos Congelados (El Marcador de Tiempo)</p>
+<p>El peligro real en montaña no es la falta de datos, sino la presencia de <strong>datos congelados</strong> [Source: 2: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] . Si una estación de esquí sufre un corte de fibra óptica en su servidor local, la API central de Intermaps podría seguir respondiendo con el último estado registrado (por ejemplo, indicando que el remonte de Morgins está &quot;Abierto&quot;) cuando en realidad ha cerrado debido a un repentino temporal de viento.</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>El cálculo de frescura (Δt):</strong> El software de LyAi extrae el campo <code>timestamp</code> del cuerpo de la respuesta de la API [Source: 2: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] . Compara este valor con el reloj interno del servidor LyAi ($Tactual​$).-   <strong>El umbral de veto (60 minutos):</strong> Si la diferencia de tiempo ($Δt=Tactual​−TAPI​$) supera los 60 minutos, el sistema clasifica de inmediato la fuente de datos de ese sector o estación como <strong>&quot;No Fiable&quot;</strong>.</li>
+</ul>
+<p>3. Ejecución del Fallback de Seguridad</p>
+<p>En el momento en que se activa el veto por datos obsoletos ($Δt&gt;60$ min) o por pérdida de conexión directa con la API, el sistema ejecuta de forma automática tres acciones de protección civil y responsabilidad legal:</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>Aislamiento del Sector (Veto Físico):</strong> El peso de todas las aristas asociadas a la estación o sector afectado por el fallo de datos se modifica a infinito (<code>∞</code>) en el motor de cálculo. El ruteador asume de forma preventiva que esas pistas y remontes están <strong>cerrados</strong>, impidiendo que se recomiende a un esquiador descender hacia un sector del que no se conoce con certeza su estado operativo actual.-   <strong>UI Dinámica de Advertencia:</strong> En el front-end del usuario (WebApp de marca blanca), la visualización de la pista o remonte pasa de verde/rojo a un sombreado gris o amarillo difuminado. Se despliega un banner de advertencia destacado que indica: <strong>&quot;Estado de montaña en verificación&quot;</strong> [Source: 1: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] .-   <strong>Cesión del Canal a los Pisters Oficiales:</strong> De acuerdo con las salvaguardas de seguridad de LyAi, la plataforma renuncia a interpretar o predecir las condiciones de la montaña [Source: 5: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] . El banner dinámico de advertencia incorpora un botón de redirección inmediata que carga de manera literal el <strong>Boletín de Pistas Oficial</strong> en formato texto o PDF emitido directamente por los pisters en su última ronda física [Source: 5: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] [Source: 6: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>
+<p>4. Registro de Auditoría Inmutable</p>
+<p>Toda transición de estado (Verde a Amarillo), fallo de conexión o activación de la regla de veto queda registrada de forma inmutable en la base de datos de administración de la plataforma. Este registro almacena:</p>
+<ul>
+<li>La hora exacta del fallo ($Tactual​$).-   La última respuesta recibida de la API y su marca de tiempo ($TAPI​$).-   El alcance geográfico del veto (estaciones y remontes afectados).</li>
+</ul>
+<p>Este registro digital constituye la <strong>defensa judicial del consorcio esquiador</strong> ante posibles reclamaciones por accidentes o rescates, demostrando que la plataforma actuó con la máxima diligencia y bloqueó preventivamente las rutas en el minuto exacto en que los datos externos perdieron fiabilidad [Source: 7: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] .</p>

Para proteger al esquiador, el sistema bloquea automáticamente el itinerario afectado por seguridad, muestra un aviso destacado de color amarillo que indica <strong>&quot;Estado de montaña en verificación&quot;</strong> y redirige la consulta al boletín de pistas oficial emitido en vivo por el servicio de pistas local [Source: 7: terminos-referencia-integracion.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>

+<ul>
+<li><strong>Autenticación Delegada (Acceso C):</strong> LyAi descarta estrictamente la captura directa o almacenamiento de credenciales de usuario del consorcio [Source: 3: estudio-profundo-modelos-negocio-lyai.pdf] [Source: 8: analisis-roi-correo-mitigacion.pdf] . La plataforma implementa un flujo de Autenticación Delegada mediante el protocolo estándar <strong>OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect</strong> [Source: 8: analisis-roi-correo-mitigacion.pdf] [Source: 10: qa-preparacion-reunion-fabrice.pdf] .-   <strong>Protección de Contraseñas:</strong> El visitante inicia sesión directamente en el servidor oficial de seguridad del dominio [Source: 8: analisis-roi-correo-mitigacion.pdf] [Source: 11: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] . LyAi únicamente recibe de vuelta un token firmado digitalmente para autorizar el proceso de compra con un solo gesto, garantizando que el software de LyAi nunca visualice la contraseña privada del cliente [Source: 8: analisis-roi-correo-mitigacion.pdf] [Source: 11: LyAi_PdS_Dossier_ES_2026-08-03.pdf] .-   <strong>Soberanía de Datos:</strong> Toda la infraestructura tecnológica autogestionada por LyAi reside de forma exclusiva en servidores ubicados dentro del <strong>Espacio Económico Europeo (EEE)</strong> [Source: 12: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] [Source: 13: LyAi_PdS_Anexo_ES_2026-08-12.pdf] .</li>

+<hr>
+<p>DOSSIER DE JUSTIFICACIÓN TÉCNICA Y OPERATIVA (INTERREG / FEDER)</p>
+<p><strong>Marco de Financiación de la Unión Europea 2021-2027</strong> <strong>Programas de Referencia:</strong> <em>Interreg Europe – Smart Tour</em>, <em>DESTI-SMART</em> y <em>Fondos de Desarrollo Regional (FEDER)</em> [Source: 3: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 4: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .</p>
+<hr>
+<p>1. Ficha Técnica de Codificación del Proyecto</p>
+<p>Para que la solicitud sea admitida a trámite, la entidad gestora del consorcio transfronterizo (como <strong>PNT d.o.o.</strong> en los Alpes Julianos [Source: 5: simulacion-ingresos-julian-alps.pdf] , la <strong>GmbH</strong> en Austria [Source: 6: organizacionesJSON.pdf] o la <strong>Compagnie des Pyrénées</strong> en Francia [Source: 7: INFORME.md] ) debe codificar la adquisición de la plataforma bajo la siguiente estructura oficial de la convocatoria [Source: 2: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] :</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>Línea Temática Elegible:</strong> <em>Smart and Connected Borders / Smart Tourism</em> (Turismo Inteligente y Movilidad Conectada) [Source: 3: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 4: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .-   <strong>Paquete de Trabajo Sugerido:</strong> <strong>Work Package 3 (WP3) – &quot;Infraestructura Tecnológica e Integración Turística Transfronteriza&quot;</strong> [Source: 2: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .-   <strong>Modalidad de Contratación:</strong> Licencia de Software como Servicio (SaaS) mediante un canon fijo institucional anual [Source: 2: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .-   <strong>Nivel de Cofinanciación Admitido:</strong> Entre el <strong>75% y el 80% del valor total del contrato</strong>, lo que reduce drásticamente el coste de inversión neta para los operadores locales y el consorcio [Source: 2: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>
+<hr>
+<p>2. Memoria Justificativa de Elegibilidad: Los Tres Pilares de LyAi</p>
+<p>La Comisión Europea exige que todo proyecto tecnológico financiado demuestre un impacto real en la cohesión del territorio y la interoperabilidad de servicios. El software de LyAi se justifica formalmente bajo tres pilares de innovación [Source: 8: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] :</p>
+<p>Pilar A: Cohesión Financiera y &quot;Smart Settlement&quot; (Smart Governance)</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>El Problema Territorial:</strong> Las alianzas multiestación y transfronterizas que comparten un pase único (como el <em>Julian Alps Ski Pass</em> que une a Eslovenia, Italia y Austria [Source: 5: simulacion-ingresos-julian-alps.pdf] ) sufren de manera histórica disputas internas, falta de transparencia y una costosa carga administrativa para auditar y repartir de forma equitativa el dinero recaudado por el forfait común [Source: 8: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 9: analisis-roi-correo-mitigacion.pdf] . Los modelos analógicos tradicionales basados en declaraciones manuales o estimaciones estadísticas de afluencia son propensos a ineficiencias o fraudes de declaración, tal y como reveló de manera pública la auditoría del diario <em>24 heures</em> sobre las estaciones socias de la cooperativa suiza <strong>Magic Pass</strong> [Source: 8: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 10: estudio-profundo-modelos-negocio-lyai.pdf] .-   <strong>La Solución Tecnológica:</strong> El módulo <strong>Smart Settlement</strong> de LyAi actúa como un auditor digital neutro en la nube [Source: 8: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] . Al conectarse de forma pasiva a los registros de pasos por torno, recopila y procesa las validaciones RFID individuales (anonimizadas bajo SHA-256 para cumplir estrictamente con el RGPD), calculando matemáticamente y en tiempo real el reparto monetario exacto según el uso real del esquiador en cada remonte [Source: 8: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] . Al automatizar este proceso, <strong>se reducen en más de un 80% los costes y horas de consultoría y auditoría de cierre de temporada</strong>, garantizando la paz societaria y la transparencia contable exigida para fondos públicos [Source: 8: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 11: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>
+<p>Pilar B: Eliminación de Barreras Físicas e Interoperabilidad Tecnológica</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>El Problema Territorial:</strong> Las estaciones transfronterizas operan con proveedores de control de accesos físicamente incompatibles [Source: 11: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] . Por ejemplo, en <strong>Ski amadé</strong> conviven terminales de <strong>SKIDATA</strong> y de <strong>Axess</strong> de manera mixta [Source: 6: organizacionesJSON.pdf] . Para un consorcio de montaña, forzar la unificación tecnológica obligando a los socios locales a cambiar sus tornos físicos para adoptar un solo fabricante exige inversiones de capital (CAPEX) millonarias que resultan inviables [Source: 11: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .-   <strong>La Solución Tecnológica:</strong> LyAi unifica de manera lógica estos ecosistemas sin tocar el hardware [Source: 12: notebooklm-conversation-european-ski-organizations-performance-and-ranking-2026-08-30.md] [Source: 13: qa-preparacion-reunion-fabrice.pdf] . El software actúa como un traductor universal que normaliza y unifica las bases de datos de validaciones y de billete de SKIDATA y Axess bajo un único modelo de datos unificado en la nube [Source: 14: terminos-referencia-integracion.pdf] [Source: 15: terminos-referencia-integracion.pdf] . Esto protege al 100% la inversión pública previa de las estaciones asociadas y elimina de forma definitiva la barrera de acceso del usuario final, que puede utilizar un único soporte digital en todo el dominio transfronterizo [Source: 3: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 11: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>
+<p>Pilar C: Creación del Primer Modelo de &quot;Open Data&quot; de Montaña en la UE</p>
+<ul>
+<li><strong>El Problema Territorial:</strong> La Unión Europea prioriza de manera absoluta la creación de infraestructuras de datos interoperables bajo el <em>Espacio Común Europeo de Datos de Turismo</em> [Source: 16: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] . Sin embargo, la prospección de mercado de LyAi sobre <strong>84 organizaciones de esquí europeas constató que ningún dominio ofrece actualmente una API pública ni datos operacionales abiertos (Open Data)</strong>, lo que perpetúa un aislamiento digital absoluto frente a las redes de movilidad urbana y regional [Source: 16: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] [Source: 17: notebooklm-conversation-european-ski-organizations-performance-and-ranking-2026-08-30.md] .-   <strong>La Solución Tecnológica:</strong> Al implementar la capa de marca blanca de LyAi, el consorcio abre un portal unificado de <strong>Open Data operacional</strong> [Source: 16: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] . Esto permite exportar de forma controlada indicadores de uso de remontes, flujos de afluencia de esquiadores en pista y datos de movilidad de lanzaderas terrestres en vivo (como el sistema transfronterizo <strong>ÉVA&#39;D</strong> en Portes du Soleil) directamente a los portales de transporte y turismo regionales de la UE [Source: 16: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] . Esta innovación convierte al proyecto en un caso de éxito pionero, demostrativo y reproducible a escala comunitaria [Source: 16: justificantes-fondos-interreg.pdf] .</li>
+</ul>
+<hr>
